!45 = !{!"/app/example.hlsl", !"//==========================================================================//\0A// Two spellings of the same shader, side by side. The first two panes compile the\0A// by-value form (the struct element is passed as a function argument); the third\0A// compiles the direct-indexing form.\0A//\0A// In the by-value panes, both structured-buffer loads sit in the entry block, above\0A// the single conditional branch, and the two [branch] conditions have been folded\0A// into one. In the direct-indexing pane the integer load comes first, then a\0A// conditional branch, and only then the float load -- so that load runs only when the\0A// first condition holds. The reported cost is that one load in the by-value form.\0A//\0A// Both forms are correct code; the difference is where the memory access ends up.\0A// Compare the position of the float-typed load relative to the first conditional\0A// branch in each pane.\0A//\0A// Compiler Explorer builds these with debug flags appended, which changes value names\0A// and adds metadata but not the placement being compared. Verified locally on a Debug\0A// build of main and on 20 stable releases back to v1.4.1907.\0A//==========================================================================//\0A\0Astruct SData\0A{\0A\09float3 value;\0A\09uint type;\0A\09float4 value2;\0A};\0A\0AStructuredBuffer<SData> dataBuffer;\0A\0Avoid fct1(SData data)\0A{\0A\09[branch]if (data.type == 0)\0A\09\09[branch] if(data.value.x < 0.0f)\0A\09\09\09discard;\0A}\0A\0Avoid test1()\0A{\0A\09fct1(dataBuffer[0]);\0A}\0A\0Avoid fct2(int id)\0A{\0A\09[branch] if (dataBuffer[id].type == 0)\0A\09\09[branch] if (dataBuffer[id].value.x < 0.0f)\0A\09\09      discard;\0A}\0A\0Avoid test2()\0A{\0A\09fct2(0);\0A}\0A"}
